summary: The door's missing census verbs land as RECORDING ARMS on the truck drop-in executor binding (corpus/ttc/door.py records construction rows; truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs computes exact facts over the recorded carriers, FH-SPLINE-LATHE's revolve arm as template). Landed: (1) the extrude arm — a closed planar line-loop profile swept along its own plane normal is an exact prism (volume = profile area x swept length; the real Merlin thrust-cone gusset row reproduces OCC's plate exactly: kernel volume 175680.0 and y-extent [-9,9] equal the OCC build123d measurement); (2) the loft arm — an ordered section stack of matched closed line-loops with exact divergence-form boundary-integral volume over the ruled faces; the degenerate two-section identical-section case is a prism whose volume is bit-identical to the extrude arm, and a coaxial similar-section pair reproduces the pyramid-frustum closed form h/3(A0 + A1 + sqrt(A0 A1)) — the same algebraic special case as the lathe line-profile frustum telescoping, which stays bit-identical (regression); (3) the sweep-as-loft-chain closed (halo) form — a closed station list certifies its seam with the exact aligned-meeting-edge identity A0 W1 - A1 W0 == 0 (reported as seam_mismatch 0.0) and a non-closing chain refuses typed with the mismatch evidence; (4) the mirror arm — mirror_y (and the YZ/XY planes) records a placed-carrier reflection over the mirrored row: the solid spec is untouched, facts transform with the placement, no geometry is recomputed; (5) make_face extension — a closed wire (line or spline-trimmed) records a planar Face whose elementary surface and trim boundary the kernel derives exactly (no flattening). Refusals stay typed and unchanged in vocabulary: partial-arc/unsupported carriers use the mapped Refused class; the loft/sweep/mirror refusal literals are preserved exactly once each (anchors A2-A4). The line-profile revolve arm's landed behavior is untouched (bit-identical regression re-verified through the native module).

implementation.bridge_types: truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs: SolidSpec gains `Prism { profile: Vec<ProfileEdge>, amount, both }` (a new 3-D profile carrier ProfileEdge = line endpoints / spline defining samples) and `Loft { sections: Vec<Vec<ProfileEdge>>, closed }`. PartSpec gains an optional placed-carrier `mirror` ("x"/"y"/"z", serde-defaulted so existing rows are untouched). Facts gain `seam_mismatch: Option<f64>`, serialized by bd_facts only when a single closed halo loft row is measured. No new base Refusal variants; out-of-envelope forms return UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier) exactly as before.
implementation.prism_facts: The profile's right-hand area vector fixes the plane normal; the volume is the polygon area times the swept length (`amount` one-sided along +normal, `2*amount` symmetric for `both` — the OCC Face-normal extrusion convention, measured against build123d on the real gusset: both=True on the tri gives y in [-9,9] and volume = A*18). bbox = the profile support widened along the normal; the mesh sweeps the boundary between the two end planes plus cap fans (deterministic).
implementation.loft_facts: Per consecutive section pair the ruled matched-vertex interpolation makes the cross-section polygon area a quadratic of the stack parameter, so the volume is the exact divergence-form integral over the loft's faces: each ruled side patch between matching edges contributes the exact bilinear moment (1/3) int int X.(Xu x Xv) du dv evaluated by two-point Gauss-Legendre (the integrand is a polynomial of degree (2,2)), and each open-chain end cap contributes (1/3) d A. This is the segment-moment generalisation of the line-profile revolution: the landed frustum telescoping is the degenerate two-section case, and for two identical sections the arm reduces to the prism value bit-for-bit (machine-checked). The bbox is exactly the section-vertex envelope (the support of any axis-linear function over a matched ruled chain is attained at a station vertex). A closed halo row has no caps; its last station returns exactly to the first, and the arm certifies the seam identity on the aligned meeting edges (weights 1 for the recorded line carrier), refusing typed on a mismatch.
implementation.mirror_arm: mirror(shape, about=Plane.XZ/YZ/XY) returns a row carrying the same solid spec plus the mirror placed-carrier reflection; the frame translation is reflected and rz negated for the anti-commuting x/y reflections so the world reflection about the origin plane composes exactly with the recorded rz translation. Facts: volume unchanged, bbox reflected, mesh reflected — no geometry recomputation.
implementation.door_recording: corpus/ttc/door.py: make_face records a Face from a closed wire (spline trims kept as samples); extrude records a `prism` row for a Face line-loop carrier (spline-trimmed faces refuse typed); loft records a `loft` row from an ordered Face list; sweep keeps the anchored typed refusal (its closed chain form is the bridge Loft row); mirror records the placed carrier; Edge gains position_at/tangent_at answering exactly as data at the recorded start and refusing typed for a spline-path tangent (the FH tube() rows' untyped AttributeError DNF is closed: they now refuse with the mapped Refused class). Plane exposes XZ/YZ/XY coordinate-plane markers for the mirror arm. Anchors: 'enum SolidSpec' x1; 'loft is not a kernel-engine row' x1; 'sweep is not a kernel-engine row' x1; 'mirror is not a kernel-engine row' x1.

findings.detail: `mvac_row_still_refuses_typed_at_the_extrude_carrier` (truck123d/tests/ttc_lathe_spline.rs, not in this packet's write set) pinned mvac's first refusal at the thrust-structure gusset extrude. The FH-CENSUS adjudication folded the extrude carrier into this packet (scope 6a, 'the extrude handler becomes a recording arm'), so the gusset now records and mvac proceeds past authoring to refuse typed at the later non-z Location placement. The stale pin therefore fails (message is now the Location refusal). findings.title: Spline-section loft facts stay typed refusals; the spline-section exact-volume derivation is the admission program's T2'
findings.detail: The loft arm records any Face-section stack (line or spline carriers, no flattening) but computes exact facts only for the machine-checkable matched line-section ruled class (its divergence-form derivation is checked against independent Simpson / closed-form frustum / Gauss quadrature in the tests). A spline-section loft is recorded and then refuses typed at the facts arm rather than being approximated: its exact volume over tensor-spline faces is T2' (the SWEPT_PAIR_ADMISSION_SPEC certified-volume deliverable), out of this packet's authoring scope. This is the recorded boundary, not a reduction failure: every corpus construction reduces to its census rows.
findings.evidence: SolidSpec::Loft over spline sections returns UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier) from solid_volume (profile_loop on a spline edge); the halo seam certificate is independent of the volume envelope and is certified on the recorded closed station chain.
